Though, I did come up with another wonderful test that people can do! I was thinking of ways that people could have fun proving it to themselves. Not only does it show that the earth is a sphere, it shows that the planet is an oblate spheroid. You can easily confirm it, with just a couple of days and a few hundred dollars.

Get a scale that is accurate to five decimal places. Order a stand for it. Order a scientific 5kg weight.

Weigh the weight at your current location.

If you're near the equator, go a day's travel towards the poles. Either way works. Weigh the weight again. Then, go one more day, and weigh the weight again. Try to do them at about the same elevation above sea level. If you're nearer to the poles, do it in the opposite direction.

The force of gravity will be lower near the equator, by a small amount. The mass of the weight will remain the same, but it will register differently on the scale. The further you move from the equator, the greater the weight will be on the scale. This is because the planet is fatter around the middle, meaning you're further away from the center of the planet and thus are less affected by the gravitational pull of the earth's mass!

Just a day's travel will be far enough to show on a scale that is accurate to five decimal points. Tada!

Why yes, yes I do spend way too much time pondering the universe around me. But, the only way it would work like that is if the planet were not only a sphere, but if it were an oblate spheroid! Assuming 150km distance between weighing points, and the same elevation, the difference should be no less than 0.0002 kg, though I would suggest being accurate out to five significant digits just because variations in geological features can have a slight impact.
